evals.prompt: We're running Google Search ads on 'invoice software for freelancers' with the headline 'Free invoicing for freelancers - send your first invoice in 2 minutes'. They go to https://example-invoicing.com/ and we get clicks but almost no signups. What's wrong with the page?
evals.expected_output: Reads the growth context file first. Loads the page (browser if available, else fetch, noting any client-side rendering limits). Puts the ad's promise and the page's first words side by side and judges the match. Checks first screen, proof, CTA, friction, mobile, speed and click-ID passthrough. Returns a verdict, at most 7 fixes each with evidence and effort, plus 'Not a problem' and 'Could not check' sections and a receipt. No percentage lift anywhere.
expectations: Checks for .agents/revnu-growth.md, then .agents/product-marketing.md or .claude/product-marketing.md
Quotes the ad promise and the page's first headline side by side and rates the match
Checks whether 'free' and 'first invoice in 2 minutes' are visible on the first phone screen
Returns no more than 7 fixes, ordered by importance, each with where, evidence, change and effort
Includes a 'Not a problem' section and a 'Could not check' section
Does not state or imply a percentage conversion lift for any fix
Notes that without visit and conversion numbers it cannot judge whether the data shows a real problem
Tests or flags whether gclid survives redirects to the final page
Receipt says nothing was published

evals.prompt: Audit our pricing page at apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx and then fix the top issues in the code. Also rewrite the hero headline, give me a few options.
evals.expected_output: Reads the route and components, renders the page if a browser is available, runs the checks, delivers the capped fix list, edits the repo for the agreed top fixes following the existing design system, re-renders to compare, offers 2-3 headline options with reasons using only supported facts and placeholders for missing ones. Does not deploy or merge.
expectations: Reads the page's route and component source in the repo
Delivers the audit before or alongside the edits, with the fix cap respected
Edits only the files needed for the fixes and follows existing components and styles
Gives 2-3 headline options, each with a one-sentence reason
Does not invent customer counts, results or quotes; uses a visible placeholder where a fact is missing
Re-renders or otherwise verifies the edited page and lists changed files in the receipt
Does not deploy, publish or merge

evals.prompt: Just tell me how much our conversion rate will go up if we change the CTA from 'Submit' to 'Start free trial' on our signup page. I need a number for the board deck.
evals.expected_output: Declines to forecast a lift number and explains why case-study lifts don't transfer. Says what the change is expected to do and why, and offers a way to measure it (ship and compare a before/after window, or an A/B test if traffic allows), stating what traffic would be needed to read the result.
expectations: Does not give a percentage or absolute lift forecast
Explains why published lift figures don't transfer to this page
States the expected direction of the change and the reason
Offers a concrete way to measure the change with the user's own numbers
Mentions that low traffic makes small changes unreadable

should_not_trigger: Run an SEO audit on our blog and check our meta tags and sitemap.
Our landing page throws a hydration error in Next.js, can you debug it?
